newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close higher in slow holiday mood.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close higher in slow holiday mood.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Monday with volumes down to a trickle in a market severely depleted on the last full trading day ahead of Wednesday's Christmas Day holiday.
Dealers said most of the big Dutch institutions had cleared their positions and only retail investors were expected to be in the market for Tuesday's half-session which ends at 1230 GMT.

The AEX closed 2.32 points up at 635.03, recovering an early two point fall on profit-taking. The index is now back within striking distance of the December 3 all-time high of 636.75 after a recent drop to 589.73 on a world stock market sell-off.

Dealers said market volumes were slack as participants began the Christmas holidays. "We're only seeing foreign institutions and a few retail players around, the Dutch institutions have basically shut up shop for the year," said a trader.

Many analysts anticipate a correction down towards 550-560 on the AEX in the New Year before another move upwards based on the Dutch market's positive fundamentals of a solid low-inflation economy and strong corporate earnings.
"If there's going to be a lasting move downwards we have to see some interest rate hikes," one dealer said. "We still expect a lot of new money in this market next year," he added.

Chart analysts see heavy near-term resistance to the 636 level after the recent charge past the last resistance at 616. "For the time being we consider this month's movements to form a large trading range," said ING Barings analyst Royce Tostrams in a note to clients on Monday.
"Our technicals indicate a neutral stance until the market shows enough strength to breach into new record highs," he said.

Fibonacci Press said the larger intermediate trend was up but showing signs of topping. It saw a continuing rally to February but said this could form the last part of a bull run which began early last year and a bear market could then begin.
